```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
source("AOT_partial_invariance.R")
r <- run_aot_invariance()
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = "AOT_partial_invariance_files/figure-",
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
fmt <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
base <- filter(r$comparison, kind == "Baseline")
shortlisted <- r$comparison %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("Single deletion", "Combined deletion"), valid) %>%
  arrange(CFI_loss, desc(config_CFI), desc(n_items))
best <- slice_head(shortlisted, n = 1)
partial <- r$comparison %>% filter(kind == "Partial constraints", valid) %>% arrange(CFI_loss)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
```

# Main finding

```{r main-finding, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf("The analysis uses **%s participants from %s countries**, held constant across every item subset. ",
            format(r$N, big.mark = ","), r$countries))
cat(sprintf("For the identified 13-item baseline, robust CFI changes by **%s** at the metric step and **%s** at the scalar step.\n\n",
            fmt(base$metric_dCFI), fmt(base$scalar_dCFI)))
if (nrow(best)) {
  cat(sprintf("Among the tested admissible reduced scales, the smallest combined CFI deterioration occurs after removing **%s** (%s items retained). Its configural CFI is **%s**, with metric and scalar changes of **%s** and **%s**, respectively.\n\n",
              best$dropped, best$n_items, fmt(best$config_CFI), fmt(best$metric_dCFI), fmt(best$scalar_dCFI)))
  if (best$CFI_loss < base$CFI_loss) {
    cat("This improves the selected fit-change criterion relative to the full scale. ")
  } else cat("This does not improve the selected fit-change criterion relative to the full scale. ")
  cat(if (best$within_01) "Both CFI drops are within the descriptive 0.01 reference used here. " else
        "At least one CFI drop still exceeds the descriptive 0.01 reference used here. ")
  cat("Absolute fit and the other fit indices are reported below; a smaller CFI drop alone does not establish measurement invariance.\n\n")
} else cat("No reduced-scale candidate met the numerical-admissibility checks.\n\n")
if (nrow(partial)) {
  b <- partial[1, ]
  cat(sprintf("Keeping all 13 items and freeing the loading/intercept constraints for **%s** yields metric and scalar CFI changes of **%s** and **%s**. ",
              b$released, fmt(b$metric_dCFI), fmt(b$scalar_dCFI)))
  cat(if (b$within_01) "Both changes are within 0.01.\n\n" else "At least one change remains larger than 0.01.\n\n")
}
```

All item selection and evaluation use the same dataset. These findings identify candidates for follow-up; they do **not** validate a shortened AOT scale or establish that observed country means are comparable. The search is limited to the candidates described below and does not claim to find an optimal subset.

# Identification correction

The saved metric and scalar models use `std.lv = TRUE` and equality constraints on substantive loadings, while freeing every negative-wording-factor loading through `group.partial`. In this configuration lavaan frees latent variances outside the reference country, as described in its [options documentation](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/lavaan/html/lavOptions.html). Inspection confirmed **40 free wording-factor variances** in each saved constrained model, alongside freely estimated wording-factor loadings in those countries.

This leaves the wording factor's scale unidentified: dividing its loadings by a constant and multiplying its variance by the constant squared leaves its covariance contribution unchanged (rescaling its mean as well preserves the means). A convergence flag and a successful `post.check` do not rule out this problem.

For **every model in the new comparison**, the wording-factor variance is explicitly fixed to one in every country with `NEG ~~ 1*NEG`. Its loadings remain free across countries. This identifies a unit of measurement for this nuisance factor; it does not equate its loadings across countries. The substantive AOT factor retains the original identification and equality-constraint sequence. The original configural model already fixes these variances. All three 13-item baselines are refitted here using the explicit identification convention before screening deletions. No correction is written back to `results_v2` or its saved fits.

```{r legacy-identification}
r$legacy_fits %>%
  select(stage, CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR, converged, admissible, negative_scale_fixed) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Previously saved fits, shown for provenance only. Converged/admissible flags did not detect the unanchored wording-factor scale.")
```

A numerical check in the second country confirms the ambiguity: halving the wording loadings, quadrupling its variance, and doubling its mean changes neither the model-implied covariance matrix nor the mean vector. The same scaling freedom exists in every non-reference country.

```{r scaling-audit}
knitr::kable(r$scaling_audit, digits = 8,
  caption = "Audit of the legacy parameterisation; the unchanged implied moments demonstrate the scale ambiguity.")
```

# Design and safeguards

Item deletion creates a reduced scale. *Partial measurement invariance* more specifically retains items while releasing selected equality constraints. This report tests both, using `group.partial` for the latter, following [lavaan’s multiple-group documentation](https://www.lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html).

Apart from the explicit identification correction above, the model structure is preserved: a substantive AOT factor loads on all retained items, an orthogonal negative-wording factor loads on retained reverse-worded items, and method-factor loadings remain free across countries. The six-point items are treated as continuous and estimated with MLR, with `std.lv = TRUE`. The configural, metric, and scalar steps respectively impose no between-country equalities, equal substantive loadings, and equal substantive loadings plus item intercepts. This is not a test of ordinal threshold invariance or of strict residual invariance.

Countries are selected using the original threshold of at least 100 participants. The sample is then restricted to complete responses on **all 13 original items before any deletion**, so a reduced scale cannot gain observations merely by removing a missing item. Every scored response and country ordering was compared with the saved baseline; the data match exactly. The saved baseline records lavaan `r r$baseline_version`; these comparisons use lavaan `r r$current_lavaan_version`. No `results_v2` file is modified.

The search has three stages:

1. **Single deletions:** test all 13 possible one-item deletions, fitting configural, metric, and scalar models each time.
2. **Combined deletions:** rank numerically admissible single deletions by the sum of the nonnegative robust-CFI drops at the metric and scalar steps. Ties are resolved by higher configural CFI, then item ID. Test the top two and top three items removed together. Their ranking is not recalculated after each deletion; this is a bounded follow-up, not an exhaustive search over pairs and triples.
3. **Partial constraints:** retain all 13 items and free substantive loading equalities for the top one, two, or three ranked items at the metric step; also free their intercept equalities at the scalar step. These exceptions apply across all countries. All other substantive loadings/intercepts remain constrained, and the original wording-factor specification is retained.

A candidate is eligible for ranking only if all three models converge, pass lavaan’s post-estimation admissibility check, have finite standard errors for free parameters and finite robust CFI, produce no fitting/extraction error, and have the wording-factor variance fixed to one in every country. Warnings are retained in the diagnostics. Models are not silently simplified to rescue a problematic solution.

CFI, TLI, and RMSEA below are robust; SRMR is the usual SRMR. A CFI decrease of 0.01 is shown as a **descriptive reference**, matching the original report, rather than a universal decision rule. Positive changes in RMSEA/SRMR indicate deterioration. The size and sensitivity of fit changes depend on the model and sampling conditions; see [Chen (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510701301834). Fit indices from different indicator sets are descriptive comparisons: chi-square differences and AIC are not used to compare scales with different observed items.

# Identified baseline and original-item diagnostics

```{r original-fit}
r$fits %>% filter(kind == "Baseline") %>%
  select(stage, N, groups, CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR, dCFI, dRMSEA, dSRMR) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Identified 13-item baseline on the common analysis sample.")
```

These diagnostics are conditional on the substantive-plus-wording-factor specification: a weak substantive loading here does not by itself show that an item is psychologically uninformative. The table below describes substantive-factor loadings in the original configural model. Means and standard deviations give each country equal weight. Loading dispersion is a descriptive clue, not a formal test of non-invariance: standardised loadings also depend on group variances. The final column is the RMS of the original scalar model’s country mean residuals returned by `lavResiduals(type = "cor.bentler")`.

```{r item-diagnostics}
r$diagnostics %>%
  select(item, reversed, mean_loading, sd_loading, min_loading, max_loading,
         countries_negative_loading, scalar_mean_residual_RMS) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Item", "Reverse-worded", "Mean loading", "SD", "Min", "Max",
                  "Countries with negative loading", "Scalar mean-residual RMS"),
    caption = "Original-model diagnostics by item; descriptive, not deletion criteria.")
```

# Single-item deletion screen

```{r single-deletions}
r$single_ranking %>%
  select(dropped, valid, config_CFI, metric_dCFI, scalar_dCFI,
         metric_dRMSEA, scalar_dRMSEA, metric_dSRMR, scalar_dSRMR, CFI_loss) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
    caption = "All single-item deletions, ordered by the specified CFI-loss criterion. Invalid fits are ineligible for selection.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-aot-single-deletion
#| fig-cap: "Robust CFI changes for each admissible single-item deletion. Points closer to zero indicate less deterioration. The dashed line marks −0.01; it is a descriptive reference, not proof of invariance."
plot_single <- r$single_ranking %>% filter(valid) %>%
  mutate(dropped = factor(dropped, levels = rev(r$single_ranking$dropped))) %>%
  select(dropped, metric_dCFI, scalar_dCFI) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dropped, names_to = "Step", values_to = "dCFI") %>%
  mutate(Step = recode(Step, metric_dCFI = "Metric vs configural", scalar_dCFI = "Scalar vs metric"))
ggplot(plot_single, aes(dCFI, dropped)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -.01, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_point(size = 2) + facet_wrap(~Step) +
  labs(x = "Change in robust CFI", y = "Deleted item")
```

The ranked single-deletion candidates selected for follow-up are **`r paste(r$selected_items, collapse = ", ")`**. This ranking optimises an aggregate fit-change measure; it does not mean these items are unimportant to the AOT construct.

# Removing two or three items

```{r combined-deletions}
comparison_deletions <- r$comparison %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("Baseline", "Combined deletion") |
           (kind == "Single deletion" & dropped == r$selected_items[1])) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_items))
comparison_deletions %>%
  select(candidate, dropped, n_items, valid, config_CFI, metric_CFI, scalar_CFI,
         metric_dCFI, scalar_dCFI, CFI_loss, within_01) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
    caption = "Cumulative deletion of the top-ranked items. 'within_01' refers only to the two CFI drops, not to an overall invariance verdict.")
```

```{r combined-fit-details}
r$fits %>% filter(candidate %in% comparison_deletions$candidate) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_items), factor(stage, c("Configural", "Metric", "Scalar"))) %>%
  select(candidate, stage, CFI, TLI, RMSEA, SRMR, dCFI, dRMSEA, dSRMR) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Absolute fit and within-subset changes for the cumulative deletion sequence.")
```

```{r reliability}
r$reliability %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
    caption = "Pooled raw-score Cronbach's alpha and correspondence with the original 13-item mean score.")
```

Pooled alpha and score correlations describe the effect of deletion on the observed scale, not cross-country invariance. High pooled reliability can coexist with method effects and non-invariance. Before adopting any shortened score, review the selected items’ content and translations, check whether substantive domains have been lost, and evaluate the revised specification in independent data. The conceptual scope of AOT is discussed by [Stanovich and Toplak (2023)](https://doi.org/10.3390/jintelligence11020027). Item IDs here follow the study dataset; no unverified mapping to published questionnaire wording is assumed.

# Retaining items but freeing their constraints

```{r partial-constraints}
r$comparison %>% filter(kind %in% c("Baseline", "Partial constraints")) %>%
  arrange(candidate) %>%
  select(candidate, released, n_items, valid, config_CFI, metric_CFI, scalar_CFI,
         metric_dCFI, scalar_dCFI, metric_dRMSEA, scalar_dRMSEA, CFI_loss, within_01) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Partial-invariance follow-up retaining all 13 items.")
```

The metric change is relative to the full configural model; each partial scalar model is compared with its corresponding partial metric model. These relaxed models retain more free parameters and are expected to fit better than the fully constrained versions. Improvement is therefore a diagnostic result, not an independent confirmation of the exceptions. The same deletion-derived shortlist is used for this comparison; it is not an exhaustive search for the best partial-invariance specification. Freeing constraints in the latent model does not by itself justify comparing unadjusted raw-score country means.

# Diagnostics and reproducibility

```{r diagnostics-summary}
r$fits %>% distinct(path, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(Models = n(), Converged = sum(converged), Admissible = sum(admissible),
            Finite_SE = sum(finite_se), Wording_scale_fixed = sum(negative_scale_fixed), With_warnings = sum(nzchar(warning)),
            With_errors = sum(nzchar(error))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Unique model diagnostic counts, including the three identified baseline fits.")
problem_fits <- r$fits %>% distinct(path, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!converged | !admissible | !finite_se | !negative_scale_fixed | nzchar(warning) | nzchar(error)) %>%
  select(candidate, stage, converged, admissible, finite_se, negative_scale_fixed, warning, error)
if (nrow(problem_fits)) print(knitr::kable(problem_fits,
  caption = "Model warnings and failed checks; all remain visible in the comparison files."))
```

The [analysis script](AOT_partial_invariance.R) contains the complete fitting and selection procedure. Model fits, failures, and statistics are saved separately under `AOT_partial_invariance_cache/`. The cache keys include the scored data, model specification, R version, and lavaan version. Rendering again reuses the saved models. The input files are read only; the report writes only its own outputs and cache.

Useful outputs are [all fit statistics](AOT_partial_invariance_cache/all-model-fit-statistics.csv), [candidate comparisons](AOT_partial_invariance_cache/candidate-comparison.csv), and [single-deletion rankings](AOT_partial_invariance_cache/single-deletion-ranking.csv). The two- and three-item search is deliberately limited; omitted combinations have not been tested.

```{r input-provenance}
knitr::kable(r$provenance, caption = "Read-only input files and content checksums.")
```

Render with `quarto render AOT_partial_invariance.qmd --to html`. To rerun the active search from scratch, remove only `AOT_partial_invariance_cache` before rendering. The 13-item baselines and all candidates are fitted with the explicit wording-factor identification convention, then cached. The saved original baseline is read only for verification and the provenance/diagnostic tables; no legacy source file is overwritten.
